summary: Assess feeder and transformer losses, validate utility data, and draft a prioritized reduction plan. Explore the five-day course outline.
lede: Electricity distribution loss assessment helps utility engineers trace and quantify gaps between energy supplied and recorded consumption. For distribution engineers, revenue-protection specialists, and utility planners, the course covers reconciling feeder and billing records, estimating feeder and transformer losses, and assessing non-technical loss indicators without treating them as confirmed losses. Participants use evidence, cost, impact, and feasibility to prioritize interventions and shape a loss-reduction plan.
audienceIntro: This course suits professionals who investigate distribution network energy gaps, manage loss-reduction work, or use utility loss evidence to guide engineering and commercial decisions.
prerequisites: Working familiarity with electricity distribution operations, feeder or metering records, or utility energy accounting is recommended. The exercises use spreadsheet-based calculations; programming is not required. Advanced network modelling and automated meter-data analysis are introduced at overview level rather than taught as implementation skills.
